name: rustic cobbled work yard ground autotile: rounded warm river cobbles with dark earth joints, a low dressed stone kerb rim with a 2px front face on the south edge, grass tufts at the rim, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/cobble

surfaces.part: dressed stone kerb rim, south edge front face

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile: a large cobble field with dark earth joints seen straight down, with a 1-row light kerb outline around it and a grass hole inside. The only vertical face is the 2px kerb front on the south edges, for example around rows 135-139 and around the inner grass hole. That is under 3 rows, so there is no real front face. The cobbles are drawn as flat top-down plates with no receding side faces, so the tile reads as a top-down slab, which is appropriate for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are shaded one by one, in warm browns plus some grey stones, over dark brown earth joints. The 16 visible tones per tile are well above the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is only 3%, so there are no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the joints and kerb shadow lean brown rather than black, which reads as dark_material_tone. The kerb has a light top, a mid face and a darker south face, with grass tufts at the rim, which matches the brief. Weak points: the surrounding grass is fairly sparse, with only faint tufts and about 3 tones, which is about level with the grass reference. The cobble pattern also repeats quite regularly. Neither is enough to drop it below the references.

surfaces.part: cobbled ground field (flat, seen top-down with dark earth joints)
dressed stone kerb rim, south edge, 2px front face with a dark outline below

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile, not a standing object. The cobble field has no foreshortened band, no eave shadow and no ellipse. It is a top-down texture of rounded cobbles with dark joints. The only vertical face is the thin kerb on the south edges, which is about 2 rows of light stone with a dark outline below (for example x=131 rows 34-36 and x=88 rows 2-3). That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. The grass tufts at the rim are decor. A small separate kerb fragment sits at the top right.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are individually shaded in warm browns and some grey stones, each with a highlight and a dark underside, set in dark brown earth joints. The joints and kerb edges lean brown rather than black, and the measured 0% neutral dark edge pixels agrees. The kerb has a light top, a mid face and a darker 2px south front, which reads as a dressed stone rim. Measured density is 16 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, with only 3% near-flat coverage. The main weakness is the outer grass, which carries only faint tufting and is lighter on detail than the cobbles. The kerb ramp is also a little shallower, at about 3-4 steps. Overall it is at or above the reference on the primary facts and does not look sticker-like next to it.

A careful artist would accept this next to the reference without it looking thinner or more sticker-like.
